sections.h2: Why does a Memphis house get two property tax bills?
sections.html:
Memphis sits in Shelby County, and each government taxes the same house on its own schedule. The county bill is calculated and collected by the Shelby County Trustee, while the City of Memphis Treasury bills and collects the city share. The Shelby County Assessor sets the value both rely on, and the city's own tax page says city taxes on local property use assessments the Assessor certified as of January 1.

That means an owner selling in Memphis has two balances to confirm before closing. The city bill is due after the City Council fixes the rate, which the Treasury says usually happens in mid to late June, and it turns delinquent after August 31. The county bill follows the state calendar. Ask both offices for payoff figures instead of assuming one covers the other.

sections.h2: What is Memphis like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Memphis is the Shelby County seat on the Mississippi River and the second most populous city in Tennessee. It counted 633,104 residents in 2020, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 609,647, a drop of 3.0% from the 2020 base. Shelby County, with 910,226 people, is the state's most populous county.

  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 253,120.
  • Homes lived in by their owners: 44.9%, against 54.1% countywide.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $169,000, compared with $249,100 for the county.
  • Median gross rent: $1,181.
  • Median household income: $51,736, with 23.1% of people in poverty.

The city covers about 297 square miles of land and averages 2,132 people per square mile. Mean travel time to work is 21.1 minutes. With values near $169,000, the tax bill on a typical Memphis home is modest in dollars, but a back balance with interest and fees can be a large share of what a seller nets.

sections.h2: When are Memphis and Shelby County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The two bills run on different clocks, which catches many sellers off guard.

Memphis and Shelby County billing calendar

Last day without penaltyAugust 31Last day of February
Interest once delinquent1.5% per month, 18% a yearSet by the Trustee; ask for a payoff figure
Quarterly installments (age 65 and older)Aug 31, Nov 30, Feb 28, May 31Oct 31, Jan 31, Apr 30, Jul 31

Source: City of Memphis Treasury tax information page, Shelby County Trustee FAQ and Quarterly Pay page. The county does not give a discount for paying early, and it accepts partial payments, though interest still runs on any balance left after the deadline.

sections.h2: Where and how do you pay Memphis property tax?
sections.html:
For the city bill, pay at City Hall, 125 N. Main St., Suite 375, between 8:30 and 4:30, or mail a check with the stub to City of Memphis Treasury, P.O. Box 185, Memphis, TN 38101-0185. You can also call (901) 636-7200, use epayments.memphistn.gov, or pay at any First Horizon Bank branch with the bill. A tax relief voucher cannot be used at the bank. The Treasury information line is (901) 522-1111.

For the county bill, the Trustee's office is at 157 Poplar Ave., with branch locations and a mailing address of P.O. Box 2751, Memphis, TN 38101-2751. Online payment and the payit901 app are available. The Trustee lists a $1.50 fee for an e-check and 2.6% for a card, and neither fee goes to the county.

The Trustee also offers ManagedPay, which spreads current-year tax into monthly payments through February. The Trustee notes that it does not stop interest, legal fees or court action from accruing on anything that runs past the deadline.

sections.h2: What programs help Memphis homeowners who are older or disabled?
sections.html:
Three programs are described on the city's page, and the state sets the eligibility rules.

  • Tax Relief: for owners 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled and receiving Social Security disability, who meet income limits, and for qualifying 100% disabled veterans and their surviving spouses.
  • Tax Freeze: for owners 65 or older whose income stays under the limit the state sets each year.
  • Quarterly Payment Program: for owners 65 or older who live in their primary residence and owe nothing delinquent. There is no income test.

The Trustee's page says the quarterly program needs a new application every year and that applications for the 2025 cycle open July through October 2026; call (901) 222-0200. The Comptroller's relief page points out that relief reimburses taxes already paid, so you still pay the bill.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Shelby County assessment from Memphis?
sections.html:
Shelby County's Board of Equalization starts its season on May 1, earlier than the June 1 date used in most Tennessee counties. For tax year 2026, appeals were accepted from May 1 through June 30, 2026, so that window has closed. Plan for the same spring period next year.

The board's office is at 1075 Mullins Station Road, Suite C-142, Memphis, TN 38134, phone (901) 222-7300, and there is no fee to file. Owners can file online during the season, by mail, or in person. The county advises that the assessor's value is presumed correct, so the owner carries the burden of proof, using comparable sales, independent appraisals, photographs or repair estimates.

The board cannot cut a value because a neighbor pays less, waive late penalties, change rates or grant exemptions. A written decision usually follows within two weeks, and a further appeal to the State Board of Equalization must be filed within 45 days of the county notice. The Memphis Treasury says any reduction is refunded after the appeal ends, so pay the bill on time meanwhile.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes and city charges when a Memphis house sells?
sections.html:
The city lists weed cutting, demolition and board-up, sidewalk work and anti-neglect charges as items that can show up on the tax bill, so a house with a code history may carry more than the tax itself. Downtown properties may also face Central Business Improvement District taxes.

Unpaid real estate tax goes to delinquent tax attorneys on February 1 after the taxes are a full year late, and legal costs are added. A new owner is not safe from this, because the Trustee's records follow deeds recorded with the Register of Deeds and Assessor rolls as of January 1. If the owner name on the bill needs changing after a sale, the Trustee at 901-222-0200 can update it once the change is on record with the Register or Assessor. Ask your title company to pay both the city and county balances from the seller's proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When does Memphis city property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: After August 31. The city bill is payable once the Council sets the rate, usually in mid to late June, and interest of 1.5% a month applies to unpaid balances.

faqs.q: When is Shelby County property tax due?
faqs.a: On the first Monday in October, and it can be paid through the last day of February without added fees. The Trustee offers no early payment discount.

faqs.q: Can I pay Memphis property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are 65 or older, own and live in the home, and have nothing delinquent. The city plan has four equal installments due August 31, November 30, February 28 and May 31.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Shelby County property value?
faqs.a: File with the Shelby County Board of Equalization, which takes appeals from May 1 through June 30 with no filing fee. Call (901) 222-7300 for help with forms.

faqs.q: Does a Memphis house with unpaid tax have to be sold at auction?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Delinquent accounts go to attorneys after a full year, and legal costs are added. Paying the balance from the sale proceeds at closing keeps the account out of that process.
